original.reason: The asserted upper bound f(n)≤n is not established. From f(k)≥f(f(k−1)) and f(f(k−1))≤k−1 one cannot conclude f(k)≤k−1; a lower bound by a quantity at most k−1 creates no contradiction. The attainability construction is otherwise adequately checked, but necessity and thus the conclusion are unsupported.

judgment.reason: It repeats the invalid inference that f(k)≥f(f(k−1)) together with f(f(k−1))≤k−1 contradicts f(k)≥k+1. No upper bound on f(k) follows.
The minimal-k argument has the same direction-of-inequality error: the displayed facts do not imply a contradiction or f(k)≤k.
Its proof of f(n)≤n is materially invalid: f(k) being at least a number that is at most k−1 is fully compatible with f(k)≥k+1.
The claimed contradiction in the necessity argument is invalid for the same reason: both inequalities are lower/upper bounds on f(f(k−1)), not an upper bound on f(k).
